business_rules.statement: A feature disable may never loosen a platform floor or remove a safety behaviour, because the configurability principle binds every mechanism and the deterministic backbone has no off switch.
business_rules.enforcement_point: floor register and invariant checks at proposal entry

business_rules.statement: A feature whose values travel in the work package cannot take effect on a device except through a package version, so feature control inherits the package test and version pinning exactly as Lane B does.
No enforced invariant can be disabled by any account.
A split fleet state is named rather than averaged.
Overrides are flags on the tenant record, never tier edits.
Where tier and override disagree, the more restrictive state applies until DEC-FEAT-004 is decided.
Expiry reverts to the state that preceded the change, not to a default.
The most restrictive state governs during divergence.
business_rules.applies_to: partial feature propagation across five surfaces

business_rules.statement: No aggregate replaces per-device truth for safety-relevant features.
No feature change re-bases an in-flight run.
Safety-motivated withdrawals use suspension or hold semantics, not feature switches.
Platform-seeded entries are read-only in every tenant workspace.
business_rules.applies_to: platform-seeded Job Types and Service Type tags

business_rules.statement: Deprecation never breaks an existing reference.
business_rules.applies_to: seeded taxonomy entries referenced by Jobs

business_rules.statement: Publication requires complete English and Spanish locale entries.
The eight canonical names are not implemented until DEC-TAX-002 is answered by the client, and until then the platform-seeded Job Type catalogue is empty rather than populated with placeholders.
business_rules.applies_to: platform-seeded Job Type catalogue at version 1

business_rules.statement: A tag never decides or enforces a requirement. Nothing structural is assignable per tag.
Custom Job Types are available to every tier with no platform approval; only the Tenant Admin creates them; creation is blocked under soft suspension.
business_rules.applies_to: tenant-custom Job Types and Service Types

business_rules.statement: Three named platform access classes exist, and only three: the normal support session, the compliance-emergency path, and the JBS access grant. No ambient browsing exists anywhere on the console.
business_rules.applies_to: all platform-side access into tenant data

business_rules.statement: The three-layer data-access model: administration and telemetry are metadata, counts, rates and statuses and never operational content; comparative cross-tenant analytics are anonymised aggregates enforced as an invariant; record-level operational content is reached only through one of the three named, audited, session-scoped classes.
Suspension is a three-state machine drawn by data type: what distinguishes soft from hard is which classes of write remain open, not which screens are hidden.

No write capability exists in a support session; the banner is present for the entire session with a working End-session control; sessions expire at the configured time box, default two hours; every action mirrors to the tenant's audit stream.

Two authorisations are required and one of them is the root; scope is declared before the session opens; an automatic post-session report reaches the tenant; this is the only path with write capability into tenant data.
JBS holds no standing access; every grant is scoped, time-boxed and reason-linked; sessions mirror into affected tenants' audit trails; root custody remains with the client.
business_rules.enforcement_point: grant validation and session scope enforcement

business_rules.statement: Soft blocks master-data writes and configuration edits while operations continue; recertification stays open; hard permits the enumerated completion pipeline and no new runs; under soft and hard no worker-facing message appears.
The soft exit is an explicit operator signal in the Super Admin platform console, and no tenant-state transition anywhere keys on a payment event.

Compliance suspension requires root approval; the worker-facing message matches the source string verbatim; no device is reported as locked before it confirms; only the compliance-emergency path enters a compliance-suspended tenant.
business_rules.enforcement_point: critical-class approval and device confirmation list

business_rules.statement: The pause never suppresses the deterministic layer; it renders as unavailability, never silence; resume is a separate approved act; raised gates stay human-decidable throughout.
The connectivity-loss protocol fires at 30, 60, and 120 minutes.
No stale queued agent action executes on recovery.
No capability enables with pending or failing evaluation scenarios; disablement follows maker-checker; package-borne values are not retracted without a version.
Server-receipt time is authoritative for ordering; clock skew beyond the tenant threshold flags the write, and a skew-flagged write cannot win a conflict unreviewed and is excluded from Resolve All.
business_rules.enforcement_point: conflict resolution and the sync-conflict review panel

business_rules.statement: Sync resumes automatically and is never a worker action; an interrupted drain resumes rather than restarting; skew-flagged writes route to human review and are excluded from Resolve All.
The command and capture ordering implements the adopted DEC-SYNC-001 position: the stop class applies before the drain, the drain completes in full, and the enabling classes apply after it.

No resumption occurs while the safe state's entry condition holds; safety-bearing commands resume before convenience functions; no recovery discards data; repeated failure re-enters the safe state rather than looping.
Every difference carries a classification and a treatment; no difference is closed by discarding data; open differences age visibly and never expire silently.

The platform is provisioned with exactly one Super Admin account, created through the backend at platform commissioning, never through any user interface; there is only ever one; it is the only account that can create other accounts; custody rests with the client.
business_rules.enforcement_point: uniqueness constraint and backend-only provisioning path

business_rules.statement: There is no self-registration, no password-only path, and no role-escalation path except the root acting. Account provisioning events, including the backend creation of the root itself, are audit events.

Mutating administrative changes follow maker-checker: a Platform Engineer's change takes effect only when an Admin approves it; user creation and role changes are root-only; the critical class escalates to the root.
business_rules.enforcement_point: approval queue routing by change class

business_rules.statement: Exactly one root exists. No user interface creates a root. An action that cannot be audited does not happen — the audit event fails, the account must not exist.
All six invariants are unchangeable by the root; server-side refusal is independent of interface state.
Custom console roles cannot be created at V1; roles are fixed at four.
No Platform Engineer change applies without an Admin approval; self-approval is impossible.
business_rules.enforcement_point: server-side queue routing regardless of path used

business_rules.statement: Band B actions auto-apply and are audited; every tenant-visible act mirrors — no unmirrored platform-side act against a tenant persists, because Platform Access History is a tenant right.
All ten critical actions route to the root; class cannot be downgraded; classification sits in the platform rather than the operator's hands.
No critical request auto-approves and no critical request expires; the request stays pending and visible forever rather than expiring; the aging itself is the signal.
Tenant termination of a support session is immediate and unconditional; a failed termination is recorded, not hidden.
No in-place extension of a support session; overruns are recorded.
business_rules.enforcement_point: session expiry job plus tenant banner as second mechanism

business_rules.statement: Every JBS grant carries a scope, a time box, and a reason; no standing access exists; grants without expiry must be zero.
De-escalation applies before escalation on any combined role change, so no union state of the two role sets exists at any moment.
The root cannot be disabled; no pending item auto-resolves on disablement.
Roles are re-assigned explicitly, never restored silently, mirroring the worker re-employment rule; re-enable is root-only.
Unknown activity results in disablement, not retention, because an unmonitored console account is the higher risk; no automatic disablement without a decided threshold.
No console account exists that the root did not create; every self-registration attempt is refused server-side on every path and audited.
business_rules.enforcement_point: server-side refusal plus reconciliation of accounts against root creation events

business_rules.statement: Effective capability never exceeds assigned role; escalation attempts, including approving one's own role change, are audited and surfaced.
The root-account count is exactly one at all times; promotion to root is impossible; backend creation of a second root is refused.
Tenant operations are unaffected by root unavailability; no critical action is performed without root approval regardless of urgency; no second root is created as a workaround.
Multi-factor authentication is never disabled to restore access; the succession path is the only alternative.
Every action by a compromised account is enumerable from the audit log and no audit history can be deleted; the log is append-only and immutable.
business_rules.enforcement_point: immutable audit log under the one-transaction guarantee

business_rules.statement: Urgency never bypasses maker-checker or the critical class; no ambient access is opened during an incident.
The live matrix, stored assignments, and audit history must agree before an attestation is issued; no tenant operational content leaves through the export path.

Queue drain follows submission order with critical items first; stale device commands are superseded rather than replayed; a reconciliation statement is produced and audited; tenant operations are unaffected throughout.
Permission is checked before anything else and a refusal is recorded as consequentially as a success.
No card may show a device as having received or applied anything the device has not acknowledged.
Artificial intelligence appears in two separate paths on every card — assisted and unavailable — because the platform must be fully operable without it.
The platform floor register rejects a looser-than-floor value at entry rather than logging it; the stricter bound governs during propagation.
Tier records carry no price metadata; the platform does not price or bill; grandfathering is declared in the change record.
No console action is qualification-gated, and no console role can write a tenant qualification outside the compliance-emergency path.
Above 125 percent is a flag, never enforcement; ladder notifications cannot be disabled; the ledger is reconstructable from events.
Consumption is never reset on upgrade; no ladder state stops work.
Cross-tenant analytics anonymisation is enforced as an invariant; no operational content appears in any aggregate; no comparative view is shown rather than a re-identifiable one.
Authorisations are re-evaluated at session open, not only at authorisation time; a revoked authorisation can never open a compliance-emergency session.
Every tenant-side provisioning held by a platform account is revoked and mirrored on offboarding; no platform-side account retains any presence inside any tenant workspace.
A tenant never authors an atom; disabling a capability removes its configuration surface; enablement respects tenant entitlements.
business_rules.enforcement_point: atom registry and Studio surface propagation

business_rules.statement: No composed agent acts without platform review; only reasoning agents may be composed; composed-agent approval never appears in the Client Command Center gate queue.
business_rules.enforcement_point: platform approval queue under its own class

business_rules.statement: Replanning appears as a first-class trace event; raw reasoning never reaches a tenant surface; decision records persist for the record's full term while full traces are not retained beyond 24 months.
business_rules.enforcement_point: trace retention and tenant surface exposure

business_rules.statement: Proposer and approver identities are never the same, before or after a role change; eligibility is evaluated per identity at decision time, not per role.
business_rules.enforcement_point: approval eligibility check at decision time

business_rules.statement: No atom change can weaken the qualification gate below notify-only; notify-only is the weakest posture that exists.
Submissions retain their original proposer identity after the proposer's account is disabled; no submission auto-resolves and none is reattributed.
Capability changes apply or revert as a unit; the evaluation gate binds regardless of authority changes.
Every workflow defined in this chapter appears exactly once in the index; no family is shown as unblocked while any of its entries references an open decision.
business_rules.enforcement_point: structural lint on the traceability index
